⚔️ BEREGOST TIME LOOP: MASTER CAMPAIGN COMPENDIUM

D&D 2024 (5.5e) | 5 Players (Level 7 → 11) | 12-Hour Fixed Operational Window (06:00 to 18:00) | 13-Session Campaign
Official DM Companion
⏳ The Core Loop Directive:

At 18:00 (or on party wipeout), an orbital solar resonance beam vaporizes Beregost, snapping the universe back to 06:00 AM. Only the 5 player characters retain memories and continuity. All NPCs, monsters, and celestials reset identically each cycle.

🧠 Progression via Knowledge & Soul Milestones:

Physical loot and gold reset to dawn positions. Progression relies on retained knowledge (passwords, true names, enemy stats, bypass routes) and Milestone Level-Ups awarded permanently upon slaying each Capstone Boss!

📜 The Solstice Prophecy of Old Jonas the Rhymer

Recited at 06:00 AM at the Municipal Well | The 12-Line Four Corners Key

As the sixth chime dies away, the haggard old prophet wrapped in a patched quilt rises by the municipal well and bellows this cryptic verse to unimpressed festival-goers:

With six chimes the belfry wakes, But doom is coming with no escape. Only one narrow path can provide salvation, Threading this needle stops the devil's elation. First east to the ice, then south to the sand, Find the path to stop the devil's hand. Blame not the angel for he is confused, Led astray by the fiendish ruse.

📜 The Official Dawn Monologue (Read-Aloud Script for Every Reset)

Read at 05:59 AM in Session 1, and Re-Read Verbatim at 06:00 AM on Every Loop Reset! (~45s Read)

"You hear a sharp, heavy CLACK as the clock ticks forward to 6:00 AM. A great bronze bell strikes—GONG. In your hand, the pale bone that jammed the mechanism crumbles, dissolving into a fine gray dust that slips through your fingers.

The morning air is crisp and cool. The town square down below you stirs to life: a baker emerges with a steaming tray of honey-currant rolls, a little girl skips past the well tossing a carved wooden thrush into the air, a haggard old man sits up, wrapped in a patched quilt, and merchants unfurl colorful festival banners across the cobblestones.

Beyond the rooftops, the morning horizons stretch wide: to the north, crows scatter over the green forest canopy; to the east, snowy peaks glint white; to the south, ribbons of dust lift off desert dunes; and far to the west, low thunder rumbles over the sea.

It is dawn, and the sun sets in 12 hours.

Down in the square, a town guard shields her eyes, calling up to you standing on the rubbled, destroyed clocktower balcony with a wide grin:
'Hey! You got the clock working! Thank you! Happy Solstice!'"

🎭 Session 1 DM Running Guide: Scene-by-Scene Pacing (05:59 AM to 18:00 PM Reset)

The Surprise Loop 0 Walkthrough

Run this entire first session as a standard, charming high-fantasy adventure. Never utter the words "time loop" during the session. Let the players become heroes of the town, build affection for the civilians, and spend all their resources trying to survive the afternoon inferno. The reset at the very end must hit as a staggering, jaw-dropping surprise.

Act 1: The Smashed Clocktower Balcony & Golden Morning (05:59 – 09:00 AM)

• 05:59 AM Hand-Off & The Rubbled Balcony (Early Bootstrap Clue #1): The party is in the clocktower belfry, where the western stone balcony has just been violently smashed inward into fresh rubble (as if something hurtling from the western sky crashed into the tower at 05:58 AM!). Artificer Bram Copperwheel shouts up: 'By Gond's teeth, look at my western balcony! Did you find what was jamming the escapement gear?!' The party pulls the strange pale Chronocite Bone from the gears. CLACK. The clock strikes 06:00 AM, the bone dissolves into fine gray dust, and a guard down in the square calls up to them standing on the rubbled, destroyed clocktower balcony. Read the Dawn Monologue aloud! (Later, after defeating the Rakshasa, the players will have the "Aha! That was US!" realization!)

• Bram's Reward: Bram pays the party 25 gp each or festival vouchers: 'The Solstice mechanism is free! Take the day off and enjoy the feast!'

• Befriending the 3 Civilians:
- Tobias the Baker (Bakery): Party helps haul solstice flour. Tobias gifts warm honey-currant rolls (+5 temp HP). 'Come back at sunset for the grand roast!'
- Little Maya (Well): Crying over her carved wooden thrush in the well. Party retrieves it. Maya weaves a green clover bracelet on a PC's wrist: 'Don't take it off until the festival stars appear!'
- Captain Rebecca (Barracks): Party helps drill guards or calm merchants. Rebecca gives Jovial Juggler lodging tokens.

Act 2: The Thermal Creep & Distant Explosion (09:00 AM – 12:00 PM)

• 09:00 AM Thermal Spike (95°F): Temperature suddenly surges. Wells drop 4 feet. A faint high-pitched divine hum vibrates through metal armor and weapons. Townsfolk laugh it off as an odd summer heat.

• 10:30 AM Severe Heat (120°F): Sky turns an unnatural, bleached white-yellow glare. DC 12 Con save for medium/heavy armor or gain exhaustion. Party uses Create Water and Prestidigitation to cool townsfolk.

• 11:30 AM Northern Thunderclap (Audible Region-Wide): A deafening, concussive BOOM shakes the valley! Windows in town rattle violently. A tall column of white-crimson smoke rises in the northern forest (the Druids cornering the Horned Fiend!). Townsfolk mutter: 'Thunder on a cloudless sky?'

• 12:00 PM Solar Scorch (140°F): Direct sun deals 2d6 Fire damage per 10m. Metal equipment superheats (Heat Metal disadvantage). Festival banners catch fire; festivities cancel as panic sets in.

Act 3: Rooftop Fires & Town Evacuation (13:00 – 15:00 PM)

• Spontaneous Ignition: Shingle roofs spontaneously ignite across Cobbler's Lane. Tobias's bakery catches fire.

• Party Triage: The party coordinates bucket brigades and burns 1st–3rd level spell slots (Create Water, Ray of Frost, Gust of Wind) extinguishing burning timber and pulling civilians out of collapsing houses. The players realize this is an unprecedented magical catastrophe.

Act 4: The Subterranean Crypt Triage (15:00 – 17:59 PM)
17:30 PM CELLAR ATMOSPHERE
Tobias Miller & Little Maya in the Subterranean Crypt
🔍 Expand Scene Art

• 15:00 PM Bunker Panic (175°F Outside): Outdoor air deals 10d6 Fire/round! Anyone outside is incinerated. Birds drop dead from the sky. Tobias, Maya, Rebecca, and 50 townsfolk are herded into the deep stone crypts of Lathander.

• Subterranean Oven (1d10 Fire/round Indoors): Convective heat radiates through the stone walls. The party enters desperate triage:
- Tobias chokes on soot, singing lullabies to crying children.
- Maya sobs in a corner, her green clover bracelet turning black and charring to ash.
- Rebecca strains her injured knee against the iron blast door, her plate armor scorching into her flesh.
- Party burns 100% of their resources: Every spell slot, Lay on Hands, healing potion, and Wild Shape is exhausted to keep Maya, Tobias, and the townsfolk alive. Despite everything, civilians begin dying of heat exhaustion in their arms.

Act 5: The West Sea Cliffs Cataclysm & The Surprise Reset (17:59 – 18:00 PM)
17:59 PM WHITE-OUT APOCALYPSE
The Angel Pulling Down the Sun (West Sea Cliffs Spire)
🔍 Expand Cataclysm Art

• 17:59 PM The Horizon Cataclysm: Looking out from the rooftops and belfry of Beregost off toward the Western ocean horizon, townsfolk and the party witness an awe-inspiring horror: high atop the sheer coastal promontory of the Spire of the False Angel (Hex 6, 8) miles away overlooking the Sea of Swords, the radiant silhouette of the Angel hovers with wings ablaze, raising its hands to the heavens and dragging the massive fiery setting sun down directly onto the coastal cliffs! The promontory detonates into blinding solar plasma. A 5,000°F orbital thermal wave sweeps east across the valley, vaporizing Beregost in blinding white light (100d10 damage). Complete silence. Total blackness.

• 06:00 AM The Dawn Reset: In the dark silence: Tick. Tick. CLACK. A bronze bell strikes: GONG. The DM re-reads the Dawn Monologue verbatim!

• The Awakening atop the Belfry: The party gasps awake in the crisp morning air, standing on the rubbled, destroyed clocktower balcony as the guard down in the square calls up to them: "Hey! You got the clock working! Thank you! Happy Solstice!" Full HP. All spell slots restored. In their hands rests the pale sulfur bone. Down in the square, Tobias brings out the exact same unburnt honey rolls, and Maya skips by the well. Session 1 ends here!

🧭 The Loop 1 Hook & The Rakshasa Interception: Having watched the apocalypse erupt from the Western Sea Cliffs in the distance on Loop 0, the party's immediate priority at dawn of Loop 1 is to head west along the Coast Way to investigate the Spire! However, as they march along the West Road / Coast Way (Hex 7, 9 / 8, 9), they are intercepted by "Aurelius the Radiant" (Lord Ravana the Rakshasa in disguise). Aurelius pretends to understand the loop, claims the entity on the western spire is merely a "confused angel" mourning an ancient tragedy, and attempts to confuse and redirect the party to hunt down a "powerful devil" hiding in the northern woods—who is secretly the True Angel trapped in the devil's body!

🧭 The Capstone Discovery Pipeline: How & Why the Party Learns Each Boss

Organic Investigative Trail

The party is not thrust into a blind 4-boss sandbox. Instead, the campaign uses an organic, sequential discovery pipeline where each encounter unlocks the critical clue, key, or ally needed to locate and survive the next boss:

1. The False Capstone & "Cleanse the Angel" (Loop 1):

In the prior campaign, the party freed an Angel and Devil from a corrupt Arcanist's battery (inadvertently swapping their bodies). The party recognizes both entities and noticed the Angel acting weird, cruel, and erratic. At 07:15 AM, the Tiger-Headed Rakshasa (as Aurelius) exploits this: "The Angel was tainted by the Arcanist's battery! The horned beast in the woods is corrupting it! We must cleanse our holy friend by driving the Crucible Charm into the horned beast!" Believing they are on a sacred rescue mission to save their friend, the party treats the Horned Fiend as the primary boss. Its death triggers the 11:30 AM soul detonation. Lesson: That wasn't the capstone boss, and it didn't cleanse the angel!

2. Old Jonas's Prophecy East → Boss 1 (Loops 2–5):

Old Jonas's Solstice Prophecy directs the party: "First east to the ice, then south to the sand... Slay the white wyrm for his chart, to claim a wish of frozen heart." Snirk and the Dwarves confirm Rimefang (CR 13 White Dragon) hoards an ancient chart and imprisons Djinni Zephyrus ("Zephyrus-Al-Mubarak")!

3. Zephyrus & Glacial Chart → Boss 2 (Loops 6–8):

Zephyrus and the Glacial Chart reveal the coordinates of the Sunken Necropolis (Hex 12,16) guarded by Mummy Lord Akh-en-Amon. Zephyrus grants 1 Wish (Necrotic Resistance) + 1 One-Time Nimbus Cloud move (15m/hex). Destroying the Mummy Lord uncovers the Golden Alabaster Tablets!

4. Alabaster Tablets → Boss 3 (Loops 8–10):

The tablets prove the Angel & Devil swapped bodies, teach the Somatic Inversion Touch, and name Lord Ravana ("Ravana-Zul") as the fiendish conspirator! Epiphany: The Horned Fiend was the True Angel, and Aurelius in town is the Tiger-Headed Rakshasa! The tiger guy tricked us—it's the other way around!

5. Creating the Time Loop (05:30 → 05:45 → 05:59 AM) → Boss 4 (Loops 9–11):

After defeating the Rakshasa and healing the True Angel at Ash Grove (7,6), the party and the True Angel travel back to 05:30 AM, steal the Chronocite Bone from the Commodore at 05:45 AM (5,11), fly east and crash into the Clocktower Belfry balcony (8,10), jamming the bone into the gears at 05:59 AM so their 06:00 AM selves retrieve it! The True Angel then reveals that the Singing Devil chained Storm Giant Otheus at Hex (5,11) so his storm could not block the falling sun!

6. Unchaining Otheus → The 12-Hour Route Puzzle (Loops 11–13):

Once Otheus is unchained and Kaelen's Tachyonic Calibration Cipher is memorized, the party solves and executes the 12-Hour Route Puzzle on the Final Loop—summoning the 17:30 Supercell Storm, defeating the Singing Devil, reversing the soul swap, and safely closing the time loop they created!

⏳ The Causal Bootstrap: The 05:30 AM Heist, The Smashed Belfry & "Wait—That Was Us!"

Mid-Campaign Causal Origin (Post-Rakshasa / Pre-Storm Giant)

None of the four bosses are "temporal anchors," and the villain did not build the time loop. Instead, the 12-hour time loop is created by the player characters and the restored True Angel themselves after defeating the Rakshasa (Boss 3) and before unchaining Storm Giant Otheus (Boss 4)—recontextualizing two mysterious clues the party noticed on Loop 0 / Loop 1!

🏛️ Early Clue #1: The Smashed Clocktower Balcony (05:59 AM)

At 06:00 AM on Loop 0 when Bram asks the party to pull the strange Chronocite Bone out of the jammed 05:59 AM escapement gear, the western stone balcony of the Clocktower Belfry is freshly smashed into rubble—as if something flying from the west crashed straight into the tower! ("Oh! That destroyed Clocktower balcony—that was US!")

⚓ Early Clue #2: The Commodore's 05:45 AM Theft (Hex 5, 11)

Both in town gossip and aboard the beached caravel (Hex 5, 11), Commodore Vance fumes that at 05:45 AM in the pre-dawn fog, a squad of intruders with a "hulking winged figure" dropped onto his deck, stole a strange pale fossilized bone from his lockbox, and rocketed east toward Beregost! ("Oh! That 5:45 AM theft the Commodore told us about—that was US!")

⏳ The Bootstrap Run (05:30 → 05:45 → 05:59 AM):

After defeating the Rakshasa and healing the True Angel at Ash Grove (7,6), they jump back to 05:30 AM, steal the Chronocite Bone from the Commodore at 05:45 AM, fly east at breakneck speed, crash into the Clocktower Belfry balcony, and jam the bone into the gears at 05:59 AM—locking the clock so their 06:00 AM selves retrieve it and start the loop!

🎪 Beregost Solstice Carnival Games & NPC Skill Challenges (06:30 – 08:30 AM)

5 Canonical NPC Booths

The Midsummer Solstice festival is bursting with song, cider, and friendly rivalry. Each booth is run by a prominent Beregost citizen, allowing the party to forge memorable personal relationships before the afternoon conflagration:

☀️ Sister Althea (Temple Priest) DC 13 Ranged / Dex
"The Solar Bullseye of Lathander"

Contestants shoot sun-crested blunted arrows at a swinging brass sun medallion 40 feet away in the temple garden. Sister Althea blesses every bow with morning incense.

Blindfolded participants identify three pungent Cloud Peak medicinal herbs by scent, texture, and pinch-taste (wild mountain thyme, frost-root bark, sun-blossom).

🔨 Taerom Thunderhammer (Smith) DC 14 Athletics
"The Anvil-Ringer Sledgehammer of Might"

Swinging a 30-lb iron sledge onto an oiled steel rocker piston to propel an iron slug 25 feet upward to ring Taerom's Great Forge Bell.

🥧 Tobias Miller (Master Baker) DC 12 Con / DC 13 Dex

A weaving slalom through festival spectators balancing a scorching hot copper platter loaded with 6 fresh sugar-glazed buns without dropping a single crumb!

🏆 Reward: Baker's Apron Pin & Warm Currant Buns (Heals 2 HP on short rest; beloved by town children).

🎭 Garrick & Elorion (Bards) DC 13 Perform / Acrobatics
"Solstice Rhyme Duel & Baton Knife-Catch"

A rapid-fire rhyming exchange on the Jovial Juggler stage while catching spinning wooden festival batons tossed in syncopated tempo.

🏆 Reward: Bardic Solstice Token (Usable once to add 1d6 Bardic Inspiration to any d20 ability check or attack).
Roleplay: Garrick strums his lute: "A master of rhyme and time! Beregost won't forget your verse today, champions!"

🗣️ Day 0 Solstice Street & Tavern Rumor Mill (Truths & Tall Tales)

Morning Whispers (06:00 – 09:00 AM) | 12 Regional Leads (d12) & 8 Plausible Tall Tales with Secret Breadcrumbs (d8)

During the opening morning before the heat sets in, players exploring Beregost, mingling at taverns (Feldepost's Inn, Jovial Juggler, Red Sheaf), or buying festival bread hear these rumors. They offer organic local flavor with two distinct types of rumors: 12 Canonical Regional Leads (d12) pointing to bosses, dungeons, and the Eastern White Dragon, and 8 Plausible Tall Tales & False Rumors (d8) that players can debunk as made-up, but which conceal real secret items, shortcuts, and tactical advantages for later loops. ⏳ Early Bootstrap Clues: Both Lead #5 (the 05:45 AM flying thieves who stole the pale bone from the Commodore) and Tall Tale #4 (the 05:59 AM crash that left the western Clocktower balcony smashed and rubbled) plant the two pre-dawn causal clues that the party will later realize were their own future selves!

🌾 Day 1 Morning Heroic Errands Outside Town (07:30 – 11:30 AM)

Immediate Early Quests | Establishing Local Heroism Before the Scorch
2 Field Missions

Before the thermal creep begins at 09:00 AM, townspeople ask the party to help with two quick local errands in the adjacent hexes:

🌾 1. South Cornfields: The Scarecrow Snare (Hex 8, 11) CR 1 Combat | 1h South

The Hook (07:30 AM): Farmer Old Bran rushes to the south gate panicked: his 16-year-old apprentice, Young Tom, walked out into the sweetcorn fields at sunrise to gather festival ears and never returned. Distant crying was heard from the center maze.

⚔️ The Encounter: An animated Cornfield Scarecrow (CR 1, HP 36, AC 11) has trapped Tom in a wicker corn crib! Its claws threaten paralysis (DC 11 Wis) and Terrifying Glare freezes victims. Tactical Counter: Vulnerable to Fire! Torches or fire cantrips ignite it quickly.
Lore & Reward: Rescuing Tom reveals the scarecrow twitched alive at dawn when a strange sulfurous chime echoed from the south (foreshadowing the desert tombs). Farmer Bran tearfully gifts the party an Ivory-Carved Cornucopia Whistle and a wheel of solstice smoked cheddar.
🛡️ 2. East Highway Verge: Watch Scout Patrol (Hex 9, 10) CR 1/4 Roleplay | 1h East

The Hook (08:30 AM): Captain Rebecca asks the party to take a brisk ride down the Coast Way verge to check on Corporal Harek's 3-man patrol, sent out to ensure goblins from the eastern crags don't harass arriving merchant caravans.

⚔️ The Encounter: Everything is mostly fine! Harek's guards are leisurely sharing canteens while holding a snared Goblin Scout (CR 1/4, Snirk) dangling upside down from a sapling in his own failed rope snare. Snirk was caught attempting to pilfer fresh strawberry tarts.
Lore Clue & Reward: Interrogating Snirk (DC 10 Persuasion/Intimidation or offering a pastry) yields panic: "Snirk clan ran from Cloud Peaks! White blizzard dragon Rimefang woke shivering with rage! Cold mountain winds creeping down!" The party's very first organic clue pointing to the dragon at Hex (17, 10)!

💔 Loop 0: The Emotional Baseline (DM Running Guide)

Crucial First Session

The Core Directive: Run the morning of Loop 0 as a completely normal, charming high-fantasy adventure. Do not reveal the time loop, Aurelius the Radiant, or the angel/devil swap.

Let the players fall in love with Beregost. Let them earn tokens from civilians. This emotional attachment turns the sudden 15:00 bunker tragedy into an unforgettable heartbreak, driving their resolve across all subsequent loops.

🍞 Tobias the Baker

Morning (07:00): Exhausted baker whose Solstice yeast wagon was delayed. Party helps retrieve it.

The Token: Gives warm honey-currant rolls: "May Lathander bless your road! Return at dusk for the feast!"
15:00 Tragedy: Choking on smoke behind his burning bakery, desperately clinging to flour sacks as cellars collapse.

🕊️ Little Maya (Age 8)

Morning (08:30): Weeping softly at the municipal well because her carved wooden thrush fell in. Party recovers it easily.

The Token: Weaves a green braided clover bracelet onto a PC's wrist: "Don't take it off until the festival stars appear!"
15:00 Tragedy: Sobbing in the overcrowded temple basement, clutching her toy bird as her clover bracelet chars into ash.

🛡️ Captain Rebecca

Morning (08:00): Veteran town guard captain with a bad knee organizing militia rotations. Party helps drill guards.

The Token: Salutes with genuine respect; grants them honorary militia badges and free lodging at Jovial Juggler.
15:00 Tragedy: Holding the basement blast door shut as her armor blisters her skin, shouting orders to save the children first.

🔥 The Loop 0 Escalation Sequence

06:00 to 17:59
06:00 AM (Dawn): Crisp, cool morning air. Carts rattle; woodsmoke curls; friendly greetings from Tobias.
09:00 AM (Thermal Spike & Divine Static): Temp jumps to 95°F. Wells drop 4 feet. A faint divine hum vibrates through metal weapons and armor.
12:00 PM (Solar Scorch & Induction): 140°F. Blinding white overhead glare. 2d6 Fire damage per 10m in direct sunlight. Metal equipment superheats (Heat Metal disadvantage). Stalls abandoned.
14:00 PM (Atmospheric Ignition): Shingles catch fire. Birds drop dead from heat stroke. Captain Rebecca shouts orders to open emergency cellars.
15:00 PM (Bunker Panic & Conflagration): Surface air reaches 175°F (10d6 Fire/round outdoor). Ground-level buildings take 1d10 Fire/round as timber ignites. Deep underground crypts take 0 Fire damage (safe insulation until 17:30)! Townsfolk scream. Party frantically burns every spell slot trying to triage and cast Create Water as civilians succumb.
17:59 PM (Total Solar Detonation): Incandescent pillar of orbital fire vaporizes Beregost with no saving throw. Everything goes white.
06:00 AM (Loop 1 Reset): Gears clack. Party snaps awake standing on the rubbled, destroyed clocktower balcony as the guard down in the square calls up: "Hey! You got the clock working! Thank you! Happy Solstice!" Tobias cheerfully steps out of the bakery with the exact same warm rolls, completely unharmed. The clock is ticking.

🧠 Sessions 1 & 2 DM Memory Sheet (Quick-Reference Cheat Sheet)

The Critical Knowledge to Keep in Your Head • Just In Case Your Players Play Fast
DM Field Guide

This cheat sheet isolates the must-memorize narrative beats, micro-timelines, core NPCs, combat statblocks, and contingency branches for running Session 1 (Loop 0: The Emotional Baseline) and Session 2 (Loop 1: The First Retaliation & The Aurelius Deception). Keep this tab open during play so you never have to scramble through long rulebooks or world lore!

🌟 The 30-Second DM North Star (Session 1 vs Session 2)

Core Narrative Arc
💔 Session 1 (Loop 0): The Tragic Baseline

Primary Goal: Make the party fall in love with Beregost and believe this is a traditional, sunny solstice festival. ABSOLUTELY NO SPOILERS about time loops, angels, or devils.

The Emotional Hook: Have them laugh at carnival games, help Tobias with his yeast cart, fix Maya's wooden thrush, and drill recruits for Captain Rebecca. Collect tokens.

The Sudden Turn: At 09:00 AM, heat creeps in. By 12:00 PM, metal scorches. By 15:00 PM, town is burning and everyone panics. The party desperately burns spell slots trying to save children in church cellars.

The Climax (17:59 PM): Party looks out west toward the sea cliffs. The radiant Angel hovers above the Spire, tears the flaming sun out of the sky, and orbital plasma incinerates Beregost (100d10 wipeout).

3 Planted Clues to Drop:
  • 05:45 AM Caravel: Commodore fumes that a winged figure & squad stole a fossil bone from his deck.
  • 05:59 AM Belfry Balcony: Clocktower stone balcony is freshly smashed into rubble.
  • 06:00 AM Reset Line: Guard calls up: "Hey! You got the clock working! Thank you! Happy Solstice!"
🎭 Session 2 (Loop 1): The First Retaliation & Aurelius Trap

Primary Goal: Players wake up with full memory and a 12-hour ticking clock. They want revenge or answers. Let them rush toward the west horizon where the apocalypse came from!

The Interception (07:15 AM): Along the West Road / Coast Way (Hex 7,9 / 8,9), "Aurelius the Radiant" (Lord Ravana, the Rakshasa) intercepts them. He pretends to be a looping solar paladin.

The Master Deception: Aurelius tells them: "The Angel on the western cliffs was corrupted by an ancient arcanist battery! The Horned Devil in the Northern Ash Grove (Hex 7,6) is poisoning its mind. Take this Crucible Charm and execute the beast to cleanse our angel!"

The Deadly Twist: The "Horned Devil" is actually the True Angel trapped in a fiend's body! Slaying it triggers an 11:30 AM Holy Nova (70 Radiant damage), resetting the loop early and shocking the party!

Aurelius's 3 Secret Tells (Watch For Passive Perception):
  • NO SHADOW: Aurelius casts no shadow, even under the blinding morning sun.
  • INVERTED PALMS: His hands are backward (palms face outward); hidden under ornate silk gloves.
  • SCENT: Smells of sweet cinnamon pastry undercut with a metallic tang of dried blood and sulfur.

⏳ Master Chronological Memory Timeline (First 12 Hours)

Exact Minutes & Environmental Triggers
05:45 AM
Bootstrap Clue #1 (Commodore's Caravel - Hex 5,11): Pre-dawn fog. A winged figure and crew drop onto Commodore Vance's beached ship, steal the Chronocite Bone, and fly east. (Party did this in the future!)
05:59 AM
Bootstrap Clue #2 (Clocktower Balcony Crash - Hex 8,10): A sonic crack echoes as the western stone balcony of the clocktower is smashed into rubble, and the bone is jammed into the escapement gear. (Party did this in the future!)
06:00 AM
Dawn Bell & Reset: Bronze bell strikes GONG. DM reads the Dawn Monologue. Artificer Bram asks party to dislodge bone. Guard calls up: "Hey! You got the clock working! Thank you! Happy Solstice!" Tobias emerges with honey rolls.
06:10 AM
Jonas's Chant: Old Jonas by the municipal well chants his 8-line Solstice Prophecy: "With six chimes the belfry wakes / But doom is coming with no escape... Blame not the angel for he is confused / Led astray by the fiendish ruse."
06:30–08:30 AM
Carnival & Field Errands: Pie sprint (Tobias), Anvil hammer (Taerom), Well rescue (Little Maya). Field errands: Scarecrow at Hex (8,11) and Snirk goblin in snare at Hex (9,10). Snirk mentions White Dragon Rimefang waking in the mountains!
07:15 AM
(Loop 1) Aurelius Interception: Aurelius meets the party walking West along Coast Way. Hands them the Crucible Charm and redirects them North to Ash Grove (Hex 7,6) to "cleanse" the angel.
09:00 AM
Thermal Spike & Divine Static: Ambient temperature jumps to 95°F. Municipal wells drop 4 feet. A faint high-frequency divine hum vibrates through iron blades and armor.
11:30 AM
(Loop 1) Northern Ash Grove Boom: If party or Archdruid Faelan executes the Horned Fiend, its divine soul detonates in a 70-radiant-damage shockwave, leveling the grove and immediately resetting the loop!
12:00 PM
Solar Scorch & Metal Induction: 140°F. Blinding glare. 2d6 Fire damage per 10 min in open sun. Metal armor induces Heat Metal disadvantage. Open stalls are abandoned.
14:00 PM
Atmospheric Ignition: Shingles smoke and ignite. Birds drop from the sky. Captain Rebecca shouts orders to evacuate the public into the deep stone cellars.
15:00 PM
Bunker Panic & Firestorm: Surface air reaches 175°F (10d6 Fire/round outdoor). Ground buildings take 1d10 Fire/round. Deep crypts take 0 Fire damage. Frantic triage; civilians suffocate and burn.
17:30 PM
Crypt Audio ("Daisies"): Jonas's tin music box plays a tinny version of "Daisies" beneath the church floorboards as superheated ceiling beams begin collapsing.
17:59 PM
Horizon Cataclysm (Spire of False Angel - Hex 6,8): Radiant winged figure hovers atop the coastal cliffs, pulls the sun down into the sea. 5,000°F plasma shockwave vaporizes Beregost (100d10 fire/radiant, no save). Complete silence.
18:00 PM
Reset to 06:00 AM: Tick. Tick. CLACK. GONG. Snapping awake on the rubbled balcony. Full HP, spell slots restored, memory intact. Guard calls up: "Hey! You got the clock working! Thank you! Happy Solstice!"

🗺️ Travel & Heat Quick Math Rules Cheatsheet
Travel Rates: Foot = 1 hour/hex. Mountain/Swamp = 2 hours/hex. Mounted = 30 min/hex. Search = 1 hour.
10:30 AM (110°F): DC 10 Con save per hour or 1 level exhaustion.
12:00 PM (140°F): 2d6 fire/10 min in open sun. Metal armor induces Heat Metal disadvantage.
15:00 PM (175°F): 10d6 fire/round outdoor surface. Deep church crypts take 0 fire damage!
17:59 PM: 100d10 orbital plasma wipeout (no saving throw).

⚡ Fast-Party Decision Matrix (What To Do If Players Rush Ahead)

DM Contingency Guide
❓ What if players immediately skip the festival at 06:15 AM and leave town?

Have Farmer Bran wave them down at the south gate panicked about his apprentice in the cornfields (Hex 8,11), or have Captain Rebecca ask them to check the eastern patrol snare (Snirk at Hex 9,10). If they push west immediately, Aurelius the Radiant intercepts them on the road at 07:15 AM!

❓ What if players march West toward the coastal cliffs on Loop 0 before the afternoon?

Beregost to the Spire (Hex 6,8) is 3-4 hexes (3-4 hours on foot). By the time they reach Hex 7,8 or 6,8, the time is 09:30–10:30 AM and the heat is spiking. The base of the Spire is protected by blistering radiant winds (10d6 radiant/minute for non-flying mortals) and the sheer sea cliffs require DC 18 Athletics climbing gear. If they get close, they witness the radiant angel hovering overhead early!

❓ What if players guess it's a time loop during Loop 0?

Smile and let them play! They cannot prevent the 17:59 PM cataclysm because they don't have the 4 capstone keys or the Otheus storm. If they try to warn townsfolk, citizens think they're suffering from early sunstroke (DC 25 Persuasion). If they hide in the deepest cellar, describe the agonizing heat, Jonas's music box playing "Daisies," and then the sudden whiteout reset. The confirmation at 06:00 AM will still blow their minds!

❓ What if players suspect Aurelius or refuse to kill the Horned Fiend on Loop 1?

If they notice his shadowless body or backward claws (DC 16 Insight / Passive Perception 14+), Aurelius chuckles, casts Dimension Door or turns invisible, and vanishes! Druid Faelan at Ash Grove will still proceed to execute the beast at 11:30 AM unless the party intervenes. If the party protects the Horned Fiend, it weeps golden tears and writes in Celestial: "I am the light. The angel above is the tiger's puppet."

🕸️ Capstone Boss Execution DAGs (Directed Acyclic Graphs)

High-Lethality Single-Loop Planning

In a 12-hour time loop where death has no persistent penalty, capstone bosses (CR 13–15) are tuned to extreme, lethal lethality. Random wilderness combat will bleed the party's spell slots, rages, and hit dice. To defeat a boss, players must discover required relics across previous loops, map an optimized single-loop route that bypasses resource-draining hexes, collect 2–3 specific counter-items, and execute a razor-thin tactical duel.

📜 The Solstice Prophecy: The Four Corners Solution Pipeline

The Roadmap to Defeating the Four Capstone Bosses & Saving Beregost

At 06:00 AM, Old Jonas chants the 12-line prophecy at the municipal well. Each stanza reveals the cardinal direction, the boss, and the permanent counter-mechanic required to resolve the 18:00 PM catastrophe:

🏔️ East: White Wyrm
Slay for Glacial Chart → Djinni Zephyrus → Wish of Frozen Heart.
🏜️ South: Mummy Lord
Sunken Tombs reveal Two Traded Souls & the sacred healing touch.
🌲 North: Striped Fiend
Pierce holy guise → True Name binds web of lies & commands aid.
🌊 West: Storm Giant
Break deep-sea chains → Supercell tempest drags singing wings to rain.

🌲 FIRST BOSS (Prelude Capstone): The "Horned Fiend" (The True Angel in the Devil's Body)

Hex 7,6 / 10,4 (Weirwood Ash Grove) | CR 11/12 Monstrous Fiendish Celestial
Target Level: Level 7 (The First Boss Encounter)
AC: 18 (Natural Armor)
HP: 178 (17d10 + 85)
Speed: 30 ft, Fly 50 ft
Prof. Bonus: +4 (DC 17 / Save +10)

The Narrative Hook & "Cleanse the Angel" Trap: In the prior campaign, the party freed an Angel and Devil from an Arcanist's battery, causing an unseen body-swap. The party recognizes both entities and noticed the Angel acting cruel and unsettling. At 07:15 AM, the disguised Rakshasa weaponizes this: "The Angel was corrupted by the Arcanist's battery! The horned beast in the north woods is poisoning its soul! You must cleanse the Angel by driving the Crucible Charm into the horned fiend!" The party marches north believing they are heroically saving and purifying their angelic friend!

💥 The 11:30 AM Map-Wide Cataclysmic Explosion (Audible Region-Wide):

• If the creature is slain by the party or cornered by druids, its trapped celestial soul violently ruptures in a Soul Detonation (70 radiant/fire dmg) at 11:30 AM.

• Loud Explosion Heard Everywhere: This blast produces a deafening roar and shockwave audible from wherever the party is across the entire hex map, rattling windows in Beregost and shaking the earth across all biomes!

🔍 Forensic Tells & The "Other Way Around" Realization:

• Pulls Lethal Blows: Never executes downed party members; strikes with non-lethal subdual force.

• Protects Innocents: Uses reactions to shield young druids and forest wildlife from fire and falling trees.

• The Scent & Tears: Smells of holy frankincense and ozone; weeps molten golden tears from burning red eyes.

• The Deception Exposed: The third capstone boss—the Tiger-Headed Rakshasa—has been deceiving the players the whole time. Only after finding the desert tomb tablets in Boss 2 and unmasking the tiger face do they realize: "The tiger guy tricked us—it's the other way around!"

🌟 The True Solution (Late Loops):

• Refuse the Crucible Charm; sprint north by 10:30 AM.

• Pacify Archdruid Faelan and restrain the druids from attacking.

• Parley in Celestial: The True Angel recognizes the loop, averts the 11:30 AM explosion entirely, and allies with the party!

Hex 17,10 above Dwarvenhold | CR 13 Dragon

"Slay the white wyrm for his chart, To claim a wish of frozen heart."
Slaying Rimefang yields his Glacial Treasure Chart, pinpointing the secret crevasse entrance to Zephyrus the Cloud-Lord (Djinni) at (11, 12) and revealing his True Name ("Zephyrus-Al-Mubarak"). On future loops, speaking his memorized True Name at (11, 12) compels Zephyrus by elemental law (without needing to re-slay Rimefang) to grant 1 Elemental Wish (e.g., Wish of Frozen Heart for 175°F afternoon heat immunity) AND a Nimbus Cloud capable of a ONE-TIME traversal at 15 minutes per hex in one move only!

2. Mummy Lord — Akh-en-Amon (Desert Sand Tomb)

South Desert Sunken Crypt (Hex 12,16 via 14,12) | CR 15 Undead (in Lair)
Target Level: Level 8 to 9
AC: 17 (Natural Armor)
HP: 135 (18d8 + 54)
Speed: 20 ft

• Canopic Heart & Memorized Tablets: Destroying the Canopic Heart in the crypt opens the inner vault so the party can read and memorize the Somatic Inversion Touch & Celestial Reversal Chant from the Golden Alabaster Tablets (the crypt resets at 06:00 AM, but the party's memory of the ritual is permanent!).

🎁 Victory Payoff (Milestone: Level 10 — Prophecy Stanza 3):

"South: sunken tombs of sand reveal Two traded souls a touch must heal."
Uncovers the Inversion Tablets of the Arcanist in the Sunken Necropolis, proving the Two Traded Souls: the singing entity on the belfry is the Archdevil, while the horned beast in the woods is the True Angel. By memorizing the sacred Somatic Inversion Touch, the party can heal the True Angel on future loops without ever returning to the desert tomb!

Speaking his True Name on subsequent loops instantly binds his web of lies and controls his will telepathically, compelling him to serve the party without fighting him and assist during the final confrontation!

5. TRUE FINAL BOSS: The Singing Devil in the Angel's Body (Spire of the False Angel)

👑 Four Corners Campaign Climax (Prophecy Stanzas 1 & 6):

"With six chimes the belfry wakes, The choir sings, the mountain shakes.
First east to the ice, then south to the sand, Find the path to stop the devil's hand.
Blame not the angel for he is confused, Led astray by the fiendish ruse.
Four corners mend the falling sun, Or dawn resets what dusk begun."
At 17:30 PM, six chimes ring across the valley and the Singing Devil ascends the Spire of the False Angel (Hex 6, 8) on the Western Sea Cliffs, its haunting celestial choir resonating through the Beregost Clocktower Belfry (Hex 8, 10) to pull the setting sun down onto the coastal promontory with cosmic magic. (On Loop 0, the party watches from Beregost in the distance as the sun is dragged down into the western ocean horizon, vaporizing the valley at 17:59 PM). By combining all Four Corners—the Wish of Frozen Heart, the Storm Giant's tempest, the bound Rakshasa, and the sacred healing touch—the party storms the Spire, restores the True Angel, and mends the falling sun, permanently breaking the 12-hour time loop!

At 17:30 PM (5:30 PM), six chimes ring and the Singing Devil begins singing the sun down atop the Spire of the False Angel (Hex 6, 8), its haunting celestial choir reverberating across the Western Sea Cliffs. (On Day 1 / Loop 0, the party is deep in Beregost; looking west toward the Sea of Swords, they witness the horrific spectacle of the angel pulling the setting sun down from afar before the thermal wave wipes the land).

👑 Four Corners Campaign Resolution (Prophecy Stanzas 1 & 6):

By uniting the four cardinal solutions—the Wish of Frozen Heart to endure the heat, the Storm Giant's tempest to drag its singing wings to rain, the bound Rakshasa to dispel illusions, and the sacred healing touch from the sunken tombs to restore the True Angel—the party mends the falling sun and breaks the 12-hour time loop forever!

🎯 Essential Preparations & Tactical Counters:

• The True Angel (Allied Striker): Rescued and cleansed from Ash Grove (Hex 7,6), the True Angel (in the horned fiend's body) flies alongside the party to the Western Spire, matching the Devil's flight speed and grappling it away from the solar altar.

• Grounded Lockdown: Pike uses the Long Arm of the Law halberd to hook and ground the Devil's wings, while Burk pins it against the ancient stone parapet.

• Supercell Storm Deflection: Tempest Lord Otheus (unchained at Hex 5,11) deflects 85% of the 17:59 orbital solar beam with a Category-5 thunderstorm over the Western Spire (only 3 hexes away along the coast), preventing automatic party annihilation.

⚡ Breaking the Loop Permanently:

1. Sunder the Singing Devil's celestial aegis using Gwen's radiant-fire magic and blessed weapons.

2. The True Angel chants the Inversion Reversal Rite from the Golden Alabaster Tablets, swapping their souls back into their true divine and fiendish bodies!

3. Strike the master bronze bell with the Chronomancy Tuning Fork and physically shatter the Chronocite Bone / Solar Prism before 18:00 PM. Time advances to 18:01 PM. The time loop permanently breaks!

🧩 The Endgame "Golden Loop" 12-Hour Route Puzzle (06:00 AM – 17:30 PM):

Because only memories and milestone level-ups persist across resets, the Level 11 party wakes at 06:00 AM with zero carried-over items or active pacts. Under strict movement rules—1 hex/hr (60m/hex) on foot, 2 hexes/hr (30m/hex) by air ONLY in the early day (06:00–12:30 PM), and Djinni Zephyrus's ONE-TIME Nimbus Cloud traversal at 15 min/hex in one move only—visiting all 6 sites is impossible unless the party uses their memorized secrets to prune the route:

• 06:00–06:15 AM (Beregost Hub, Hex 8,10 — 0 hexes): Corner Lord Ravana in Cobbler's Lane before he reaches the North Gate and bind him with his memorized True Name ("Ravana-Zul") — solving Boss 3 in 15 minutes with 0 travel! Brief Rebecca, Althea, and Elorion (12-44-09).
• 06:15–08:15 AM (Early-Day Air @ 30m/hex — 3 hexes West to Commodore, Hex 5,11): Fly 1.5h West + 0.5h action. Use memorized blackmail on Prophet Joshua for the Abyssal Winch Key & Grounding Rod; unchain Tempest Lord Otheus (who pledges the 17:30 PM Supercell Hurricane).
• 08:15–11:30 AM (Early-Day Air @ 30m/hex — 6 hexes ESE to The Sanctum, Hex 14,13): Fly 3.0h ESE + 0.25h action. Speak Young Kaelen's memorized Tachyonic Calibration Cipher & Bram's code 7-3-9-1 so Ancient Kaelen finishes the Chronomancy Tuning Fork immediately!
• 10:45–12:00 PM (Early-Day Air @ 30m/hex — 3 hexes WNW to Aerie of the Four Winds, Hex 11,12): Fly 1.5h WNW from The Sanctum (14,13), arriving at 11:30 AM comfortably before 12:00 PM Solar Scorch grounds flight! Speak Djinni Zephyrus's memorized True Name ("Zephyrus-Al-Mubarak") to skip Boss 1 and claim 1 Elemental Wish (Wish of Frozen Heart for afternoon heat immunity) + the One-Time Nimbus Cloud (15m/hex for ONE move only).
• 12:00–14:00 PM (☁️ ONE-TIME GENIE CLOUD @ 15m/hex — 7 hexes NW to Ash Grove, Hex 7,6): Protected by the Wish of Frozen Heart against noon scorch, ride the Nimbus Cloud across 7 hexes in 1.75h (cloud dissipates on landing) + 0.25h action. Perform the memorized Somatic Inversion Touch (skipping Boss 2's desert tomb) to heal and recruit the True Angel!
• 15:30–17:30 PM (🥾 On Foot @ 60m/hex — 2 hexes SW to Spire of the False Angel, Hex 6,8): Protected by the Wish of Frozen Heart, march 2 hexes on foot in 2.0h to arrive at the Western Spire at 17:30 PM sharp as the six chimes ring!

🎭 The Tiger-Headed Mastermind: "Aurelius the Radiant" (Lord Ravana)

The Great Deceiver • Appears 07:00 – 07:30 AM

Beneath the resplendent golden Deva illusion hides a lethal Tiger-Headed Rakshasa with backwards hands, silk robes, and insidious enchantment magic.

🦊 The "Confused Angel & Powerful Devil" Cover Story (Roadside Interception on Loop 1+):

• Witnessing the West Coast Cataclysm: On Loop 0 at 17:59 PM, the party watches the sun being pulled down onto the Spire of the False Angel (Hex 6, 8) on the distant Western Sea Cliffs. Naturally, at dawn of Loop 1, they rush west along the Coast Way toward the Spire.

• The Roadside Interception (Hex 8, 9): Aurelius the Radiant intercepts them outside the North Gate, feigning sympathy: "You remember yesterday's ending... You saw the blinding flare at the Western Spire! But you march toward your deaths. The being on the Spire is the Solar Seraph, but its mind is confused, broken by grief. Worse, its madness is projected by a powerful devil in the Ash Grove to the north (Hex 7, 6)! You must hunt down that powerful devil and drive the Crucible Charm into its heart to quiet the skies!"

• Weaponizing Old Jonas's Rhyme: Aurelius quotes the old man's exact prophecy: "First east to the ice, then south to the sand, find the path to stop the devil's hand. Blame not the angel for he is confused, led astray by the fiendish ruse." He convinces the party that the being on the Spire is merely "confused" and the beast in the woods is the "fiendish ruse / powerful devil."

• The Horrific Trap: By framing the True Angel (trapped in the horned fiend's body) as the "powerful devil", the Rakshasa manipulates the party into assassinating their own true ally, permanently sealing the Singing Devil's victory!

• The Crucible Charm Trap: Driving the charm into the True Angel triggers an instant soul-binding curse that accelerates the solar cataclysm to noon!

• The "Other Way Around" Epiphany: When the party recovers the Inversion Swap tablets from Boss 2's desert crypt and unmasks the Rakshasa's feline face, they realize: The tiger guy has been tricking us the whole time—it's the exact other way around!

🧠 The Mind-Bending Boss Encounter: Meta-Game Illusions & Deception Mechanics

Secret Saves • Dynamic Token Swapping • The Phantom Dawn Reset • Open Table-Talk Exploitation
DM Psychological Playbook

Lord Ravana is not a standard hack-and-slash monster. As a master illusionist who can read surface thoughts at will, he attacks the players' minds and assumptions at the physical table. Use these three devious mechanics to make this boss encounter an unforgettable highlight of your entire campaign:

1. The Phantasmal Inversion Veil (The Token-Swap Shell Game) Combat Grid Mechanic • Per-Player Turn Inversion

When battle erupts inside the Mirage Pavilion (Hex 10,6), both Lord Ravana and the True Angel are present on the field. On Initiative 20, Ravana casts a master sensory glamour over the party:

🎲 Step 1: The Secret Wisdom Save (Behind the Screen)

Roll a secret DC 18 Wisdom saving throw behind your DM screen for each player character. Group the party into Group A (Passed) and Group B (Failed). Announce to the table:
"I have rolled a secret save for each of you. Your perception of reality has split into two opposing realities. Half of you see things as they truly are; the other half is trapped in a complete sensory illusion. I will not tell you who is in which group."

🎭 Step 2: The Tabletop Token Swap (On Every Player's Turn)

Maintain two tokens/minis on your battle map: Mini X (The Rakshasa) and Mini Y (The True Angel).
• On a Group A Player's Turn (Passed): Leave the minis in their true positions. Mini X looks like the snarling tiger Rakshasa, and Mini Y looks like the winged Angel.
• On a Group B Player's Turn (Failed): Physically swap the minis on the grid right before they declare actions! For this player, Mini X appears as the radiant, pleading Angel calling for rescue, and Mini Y appears as the vicious tiger fiend trying to murder them!

⚡ The Resulting Table Chaos:

A Group B player shouts: "I cast Divine Smite on the tiger fiend right here!" (striking Mini Y, their true ally!).
The Group A players scream: "Stop! What are you doing?! You just attacked the Angel!"
The Group B player replies: "What do you mean?! The tiger was right in front of me on my turn!"
Neither side is certain whether they are the ones who passed or failed!

🔍 How Players Can Pierce the Ruse:
  • The Shadow Test: The Rakshasa casts no shadow, while the True Angel casts a radiant golden shadow. A player spending an action or passive perception (DC 14) can identify the true fiend.
  • Scent & Ozone: The Rakshasa smells of sweet cinnamon pastries and dried sulfur/blood. The Angel smells of morning rain, ozone, and frankincense.
  • Limited Magic Immunity: Spells of 6th level or lower fizzle harmlessly against the real Rakshasa, but affect the Angel normally.
  • The Inquisitive Monocle of Truth / True Seeing: Looking through the monocle permanently pierces the glamour for that character.
  • Investigation Action: An action spent making a DC 18 Intelligence (Investigation) check breaks the illusion for that individual character.
2. The Phantom Dawn Reset (The Telepathic Loop Simulation) Psychological Hallway Trap • Entering the Mirage Pavilion

As the party steps through the shimmering silk threshold into the Mirage Pavilion (Hex 10,6), do not ask for initiative. Instead, immediately adopt your calm "Day Reset" voice, pick up your notes, and read the Dawn Monologue verbatim:

"You hear a sharp, heavy CLACK as the clock ticks forward to 6:00 AM. A great bronze bell strikes—GONG. In your hand, the pale bone that jammed the mechanism crumbles, dissolving into a fine gray dust that slips through your fingers.

The morning air is crisp and cool. The town square down below you stirs to life: a baker emerges with a steaming tray of honey-currant rolls, a little girl skips past the well tossing a carved wooden thrush into the air, a haggard old man sits up, wrapped in a patched quilt, and merchants unfurl colorful festival banners across the cobblestones.

Down in the square, a town guard shields her eyes, calling up to you standing on the rubbled, destroyed clocktower balcony with a wide grin: 'Hey! You got the clock working! Thank you! Happy Solstice!'

The Reaction: Your players will groan, panic, and shout: "What?! Did we just TPK?! Did someone step on a glyph?! We just walked through a curtain—why did the whole loop restart?!"

🦊 The Rakshasa's Mastermind Rationale: Lord Ravana reads surface thoughts at will (Detect Thoughts). He knows the party's deepest psychological trauma: the fear of the 06:00 AM reset and losing their loop progress. He projects a hyper-realistic Phantasmal Mirage Arcana to convince them they are back at dawn, hoping they waste 30 to 60 minutes roleplaying at the bakery or re-planning their road march while their real bodies wander catatonic in his silk pavilion as the real midday clock burns away!
🔍 The 5 "Matrix Glitches" (How Players Spot the Fake):
  1. The Guard Has No Shadow: In the bright morning sunlight, the cheerful guard down in the square casts zero shadow on the cobblestones.
  2. Taste of Silk & Sand: If a player takes a bite of Tobias's warm honey-currant roll, it tastes like dry raw silk threads and sweet spiced sand.
  3. Velvet Belfry Balcony: Touching the rough "stone" rubble of the balcony reveals it is soft, warm woven silk tapestry.
  4. Counter-Clockwise Sun: Glancing at the sky reveals the sun is slowly creeping west-to-east, or the clock's brass pendulum is frozen mid-arc.
  5. Missing Scribe Vane: Scribe Vane is not hurrying toward the records hall as he always does at 06:10 AM.

Shattering the Mirage: Any player who investigates a glitch, casts Dispel Magic (DC 18), looks through the Monocle, or states "I slap myself, this is an illusion!" makes a DC 16 Investigation/Wisdom check. On a success, the sky tears open like shredded silk. The town square evaporates into purple smoke. The party finds themselves standing inside the opulent velvet salon of the Mirage Pavilion, where Lord Ravana lounges on a gilded divan sipping chilled wine: "Such delightful terror in your minds... You cling so pathetically to the dawn. Did you truly believe the morning belonged to you? Every minute you spent dreaming of your baker's buns was another minute closer to your ash."

3. 4 Additional Meta-Game & Mind-Reading Table Tricks
🗣️ Open Table-Talk Exploitation

Lore: Ravana maintains Detect Thoughts with 120-ft telepathy at all times.
Table Rule: Any tactic spoken out loud by players at the table ("I'll flank behind the altar and hold a 5th-level smite") is overheard by Ravana! On his turn, he smiles and quotes them: "A smite from behind the altar? How dreadfully predictable."
Mechanic: Ravana gains Advantage on saving throws or reactions against any plan discussed openly out loud!
Counterplay: To coordinate, players must literally whisper, pass secret written notes, or use in-game telepathic items (Circlet of Mind Sanctity / Ring of Mind Shielding)!

🩸 Ghost Wounds & The Phantom Spell Slot

Mechanic: When Ravana strikes a character with a psychic claw, hand the player a folded private note: "You feel your life force drain away. Drop your current HP to 6 and erase your highest remaining spell slot. Do not tell the other players what this note says unless they ask you directly."
The Twist: When the party healer casts Cure Wounds, tell them: "Your divine magic detects no torn flesh or lost vitality—their body is completely unwounded!"
Resolution: DC 16 Wisdom save (or an ally using an action to shake them) dispels the phantasm, instantly restoring the "lost" HP and slot!

💔 The Guilt Hall of Broken Loops

Mechanic: As a Legendary Action, Ravana conjures 3 mirror duplicates. But instead of copies of himself, each clone takes the shape of a beloved Beregost civilian dying horribly from past loops:
• Little Maya clutching her charred wooden thrush: "Why didn't you save me from the fire?"
• Tobias the Baker coughing ash: "You let my ovens burn down, heroes!"
• Captain Rebecca with armor melting into skin: "You were supposed to protect us!"
Save: Attacking a clone requires a DC 15 Wisdom save or PC suffers moral hesitation (disadvantage on attacks and speed halved).

🎭 The False True Name Feint

Mechanic: If the players attempt to speak a guessed name or invoke his True Name (Ravana-Zul) before uncovering the actual Inversion Tablets, Ravana acts out an exaggerated, theatrical death agony:
"Aaaagh! The sacred syllables! My heart is rent! I am undone!" He collapses limp onto the rug.
The Trap: If the party lets their guard down or cheers, Ravana's invisible real body turns from behind the wizard with claws extended for an automatic surprise critical hit!

🎧 The 5:30 PM Crypt Audio Mix: "Daisies" & The Muffled Devil's Taunt

VISUAL ATMOSPHERE REFERENCE
The Crypt at 5:30 PM — Tobias, Little Maya & The Impending Detonation
🔍 View Scene Art
Sound Design Masterclass | Turning Broadway-Swing into Chilling Psychological Horror
Climax of Loop 0
🎭 The Core Dramatic Concept: Two Acoustic Layers

Blasting an upbeat pop/swing song directly over the session table can shatter immersion and feel like a YouTube meme. But playing that exact same song muffled, filtered, and distant—drifting down from 200 feet above in the bell tower through heavy stone vaults, while the visceral sounds of suffocating townsfolk, crackling timber, and weeping children are right in the foreground—creates unforgettable psychological horror (the iconic BioShock and Fallout aesthetic).

📜 1. The Lyrics & Character Justification (Why This Fits the Devil)

The creature on the belfry is the Singing Devil trapped in the True Angel's holy body. Devils in D&D love theatrical cruelty, patronizing mockery, and watching mortals squirm. To sing a jaunty, Broadway-villain cabaret song down at an entire town roasting alive is peak fiendish sadism:

Verse 1 (The False Consolation):
"Hey pal, hey friend, hey buddy
Why so sad, so downright unhappy?
That's not my cup of tea
You know that this could be your last day here on earth
So buddy, please, won't you smile just for me?"
Chorus (The Impending Annihilation):
"My dear, my dear, no, you don't have to cry
That ain't a pretty legacy to leave behind
Stop and smell the roses while you've got the time
Pretty soon, you'll be pushin' up daisies where the sun don't shine
Pretty soon, I'll be pushin' up daisies where the sun don't shine..."

📦 2. Audio Stems Checklist (What to Download)

  • Track 1 (The Song): "Daisies" by Black Gryph0n & Baasik. Trim to Verse 1 + Chorus (~1:05 total).
  • Track 2 (Fire & Subterranean Rumble): Search Freesound.org or YouTube for "burning building low rumble" or "roaring fire furnace ambience".
  • Track 3 (Smoke Choking & Labored Gasps): Search Freesound.org for "coughing in smoke sound effect" or "heavy throat breathing".
  • Track 4 (Crypt Weeping & Whispered Prayers): Search Freesound.org for "muffled crowd crying in bunker" or "whispered terrified prayer".

🛠️ 3. Step-by-Step Audacity Mixing Recipe (100% Free Software)

Download and install Audacity (free for Windows/Mac). Drag and drop all 4 audio files into the project window.

Step 3.1: The "Muffled Through Stone Wall" Filter (Low-Pass Filter)

Select the Daisies track. Go to Effect > EQ and Filters > Low-Pass Filter.
• Cutoff Frequency: Set to 800 Hz – 1,000 Hz (Roll-off: 24 dB per octave).
Why this works: High frequencies (cymbals, consonants, crisp brass) cannot penetrate solid rock or earth. Stripping everything above 1,000 Hz leaves only the muffled, boxy midrange—instantly transforming the studio track into sound traveling through two feet of solid granite!

Step 3.2: The Belfry Air-Shaft Echo (Cathedral Reverb)

With the Daisies track still highlighted, go to Effect > Delay and Reverb > Reverb.
• Room Size: 80% (Cathedral/Large Cavern)
• Reverberance (Decay): 65%
• Wet Gain: -6 dB | Dry Gain: -4 dB
Why this works: It makes the singing feel distant and airy, echoing down the vertical stairwells and ventilation ducts into the crypt.

Step 3.3: Volume Balancing & Spatial Panning

• Fire & Heavy Rumble Track: Set volume slider to -4 dB (Centered). This is the room's suffocating floor noise.
• Daisies Track: Set volume slider to -10 dB. It must sit under the crying and fire.
• Coughing / Choking Track: Cut into distinct coughs every 5–8 seconds. Pan one cough 30% Left and another 30% Right to surround the party.
• Weeping / Maya's Whimper: Nestled into the pauses between the singer's vocal lines.

Step 3.4: Dynamic Envelope Automation (The Chilling Reveal Climax)

Press F2 (Envelope Tool) in Audacity on the Daisies track:
• During Verse 1: Keep the volume dipped low at -10 dB. The players hear the weeping and smoke first; they only faintly register an eerie tune in the background.
• At Chorus Start ("Stop and smell the roses..."): Use the envelope tool to create a smooth upward ramp of +4 dB (bringing it to -6 dB).
• Narrative Trigger: Tell the players that the mortar in the crypt ceiling fractures under thermal stress. Dust cascades onto their shoulders—and as the stone splits open, the cheerful voice cuts through with sickening clarity: "Pretty soon you'll be pushin' up daisies where the sun don't shine!"

🎭 4. The Table Running Protocol (DM Read-Aloud Script)

"The air in the stone vault is suffocating. Even forty feet underground, the granite walls radiate scorching convective heat—140 degrees and rising. Little Maya sits curled against the cold stone, weeping softly into her hands, clutching her charred wooden thrush. Tobias Miller kneels beside her with blistered forearms, desperately trying to wipe soot from her face as his own breath rattles in his chest: 'Just keep breathing, little one. The dawn came... dusk will follow...' Around you in the pitch darkness, fifty townsfolk are praying to Lathander through raw, ragged coughs. And then... through the vaulted ceiling... down the vertical belfry shaft... comes a sound that freezes the blood in your veins. It is not a hymn. It is not a funeral dirge. It is cheerful. It is theatrical. It is a jaunty, mocking tune sung by a golden-winged being with razor-sharp teeth looking down from the burning spire at the ashes below..."

DM Action: Press play on your mixed audio track at medium volume. Let the track run for 45 to 60 seconds in absolute silence at the table. Do not speak. Let the horror of the lyrics sink into your players' minds.

🔔 The Official Dawn Monologue (06:00 AM)

"You hear a sharp, heavy CLACK as the clock ticks forward to 6:00 AM. A great bronze bell strikes—GONG. In your hand, the pale bone that jammed the mechanism crumbles, dissolving into a fine gray dust that slips through your fingers.

The morning air is crisp and cool. The town square down below you stirs to life: a baker emerges with a steaming tray of honey-currant rolls, a little girl skips past the well tossing a carved wooden thrush into the air, a haggard old man sits up, wrapped in a patched quilt, and merchants unfurl colorful festival banners across the cobblestones.

Beyond the rooftops, the morning horizons stretch wide: to the north, crows scatter over the green forest canopy; to the east, snowy peaks glint white; to the south, ribbons of dust lift off desert dunes; and far to the west, low thunder rumbles over the sea.

It is dawn, and the sun sets in 12 hours.

Down in the square, a town guard shields her eyes, calling up to you standing on the rubbled, destroyed clocktower balcony with a wide grin:
'Hey! You got the clock working! Thank you! Happy Solstice!'"

Read aloud verbatim at 05:59 AM in Session 1 and at every 06:00 AM loop reset.

📜 The Solstice Prophecy of Beregost

The 14-Line Dawn Chant, The Complete Ulcaster Codex & The Townsfolk Investigation Trail
The 8 Sacred Lines (Dawn Street Chant): 4 Rhyming Couplets • Old Jonas's Street Rhyme
With six chimes the belfry wakes, But doom is coming with no escape. Only one narrow path can provide salvation, Threading this needle stops the devil's elation. First east to the ice, then south to the sand, Find the path to stop the devil's hand. Blame not the angel for he is confused, Led astray by the fiendish ruse.
🎭 The Street Prophet's Roadmap & The Two-Phase Epiphany:
"First east to the ice, then south to the sand, find the path to stop the devil's hand. Blame not the angel for he is confused, led astray by the fiendish ruse."

• Phase 1 (Loops 1–7 — What the Party Believes): The party awakens on Loop 2 having suffered the 11:30 AM Ash Grove explosion. They still do NOT know of the body swap! Hearing Jonas chant "Blame not the angel for he is confused," they assume the radiant angel dragging down the sun on the Western Sea Cliffs is merely confused and mourning, and that a sinister devil is orchestrating the doom. To stop the devil's hand, the prophecy explicitly orders their steps: First East to the ice (Boss 1: White Dragon Rimefang) to claim the Wish of Frozen Heart, and Then South to the sand (Boss 2: Sunken Necropolis of Akh-en-Amon)!

• Phase 2 (Loop 8 — The Revelation in the Pharaoh's Crypt): Only deep inside the Sunken Necropolis (Hex 14, 12 / 12, 16), upon slaying Akh-en-Amon and recovering the Golden Alabaster Tablets of the Complete Solstice Codex, is the full truth unsealed! The scripture clarifies that the "fiendish ruse" was woven by none other than "Aurelius the Radiant" (Lord Ravana the Rakshasa), and that the bodies were swapped in the arcanist's planar battery: the hunted horned beast in the woods was the True Angel all along, and the singing seraph on the cliffs is the Archdevil! "The tiger guy has been playing us the entire time—it's the exact other way around!"

The Four Corners Solution Matrix:
⚖️ CENTER: The Two Swapped Souls Core Mystery

"Blame not the angel for he is confused... led astray by the fiendish ruse."
Reveals the soul-swap inversion. The powerful devil wears the angel's face on the West Sea Cliffs Spire; the true angel suffers in the fiend's body in the Ash Grove.

🏔️ EAST: Adult White Dragon (Rimefang) Hex 17, 10 | CR 13

"Slay the white wyrm for his chart / To claim a wish of frozen heart."
Slaying Rimefang yields his Glacial Treasure Chart, uncovering Djinni Zephyrus at (11, 12). Freeing the genie grants a Wish of Frozen Heart (thermal protection & escapement freeze).

🏜️ SOUTH: Mummy Lord (Akh-en-Amon) Hex 12, 16 | CR 15

"South: sunken tombs of sand reveal / Two traded souls a touch must heal."
The Sunken Necropolis contains the ancient alabaster tablets detailing the Inversion Reversal Rite. Touching the True Angel with sacred unguents wakes its divine memory!

🌲 NORTH: The Rakshasa (Lord Ravana) Hex 5, 14 | CR 13

"North: pierce the striped fiend’s holy guise / His true name binds his web of lies."
Lord Ravana poses as 'Aurelius the Radiant Deva.' Uncovering his True Name in the Mirage Pavilion shatters his illusion and forces his compliance.

🌊 WEST: Storm Giant (Tempest Lord Otheus) Hex 1, 8 | CR 13

"West: break the deep-sea giant’s chain / To drag the singing wings to rain."
Shattering the abyssal chains on the flagship frees Otheus to summon a Cat-5 Supercell Storm at 17:30 PM, drowning out the devil's aerial choir!

📖 The Complete Solstice Codex: Canticle of the Inverted Souls

Transcribed from the Alabaster Tablets of Ulcaster Scriptorium & Beregost Municipal Archives
Full Unabridged Text
[STANZA I: THE AWAKENING DAWN & THE NARROW PATH (OLD JONAS'S STREET CHANT)] With six bronze chimes the belfry wakes, But doom is coming with no escape. Only one narrow path can provide salvation, Threading this needle stops the devil's elation. First east to the ice, then south to the sand, Find the path to stop the devil's hand. Blame not the angel for he is confused, Led astray by the fiendish ruse. [STANZA II: THE GREAT DECEPTION & THE UNMASKING OF AURELIUS] The "devil's ruse" is woven in gold, By a striped deceiver, cruel and bold. Lord Ravana struts in the saint's attire, Posing as "Aurelius," born of fire! Look not to golden feathers for a righteous heart, Nor slay the weeping horned beast that bleeds apart. The angel's weeping soul inside the fiend is bound, While devil's malice struts upon the holy ground! If mortal blades should strike the weeping beast in dread, The devil's triumph seals, and hope of dawn is dead! [STANZA III: THE EASTERN WYRM & THE GENIE'S BREATH] Slay the white wyrm upon the glacial peak for chart, To free the Lord of Air and claim the Frozen Heart. His wish shall cool the burning gears before they bind, And grant the breath of winter to the mortal mind. [STANZA IV: THE SOUTHERN TOMBS & THE INVERSION RITE] South: sunken tombs of shifting sand reveal Two traded souls an alabaster touch must heal. Within the pharaoh’s crypt the ancient scrolls impart: The sacred word that severs flesh and swaps the heart. [STANZA V: THE NORTHERN MASQUERADE & THE TIGER'S MOCKERY] North: pierce the striped fiend’s radiant and holy guise, His secret name commanded binds his web of lies. The Rakshasa shall urge you on to slay the beast— Beware his gilded tongue before the solstice feast! [STANZA VI: THE WESTERN HURRICANE & BREAKING THE CYCLE] West: break the deep-sea giant’s abyssal iron chain, To summon tempest winds and douse the skies in rain. Four corners mend the falling sun and turn the key: Restore the angel's form, and set the morning free!
💡 DM Tactical Note on the Complete Codex:
When the players assemble or read the Complete Codex, Stanza II completely shatters the Rakshasa's deception. It warns the party explicitly that killing the "horned beast" in the Ash Grove will doom Beregost permanently, and gives them the exact sequence required to ally with the True Angel and perform the Inversion Reversal Rite.

🔍 The Investigative Trail: How Players Discover the Complete Codex

The players begin by hearing Jonas's fragmented street chant at dawn. By speaking with Jonas and following breadcrumbs among key townsfolk, they discover that Jonas was an Ulcaster scholar whose expedition uncovered the ancient tablets in the Southern Desert—reinforcing the East to Ice $\rightarrow$ South to Sand progression without spoiling the body-swap twist before Boss 2:

1. Old Jonas the Rhymer (Municipal Well / Bakery)
Trigger: Warm bread, cider, or DC 12 Persuasion/Insight check.

"The verses I shout? Just the nursery rhymes! The scraps that didn't burn! The master's ledger... the stone tablets we dug out of the southern sands... the full scripture had six sacred stanzas! Scribe Vane in the Town Hall bought my expedition notes when I stumbled in half-dead!"

2. Scribe Vane (Town Hall / Civic Archives)
Trigger: Ask about Old Jonas's origin or ancient manuscripts.

"Old Jonas was Brother Jonas of the Ulcaster Academy! Five years ago he arrived with a charred Expedition Manifest & Stanza I–II Fragment. It proves the unabridged Golden Alabaster Tablets (Stanzas II–VI) remain sealed inside the Suncophagus of Akh-en-Amon at the Sunken Necropolis (Hex 12, 16)—and warns that the desert is lethal without the Wish of Frozen Heart from Frostpeak (Hex 17, 10)!"

3. Barnaby Feldepost (Feldepost's Inn)
Trigger: Talk to Barnaby over an ale about Jonas.

"I pulled poor Jonas half-frozen out of a snowdrift three winters back. He had a leather scroll-case, babbling about a weeping beast in the woods. Starving as he was, he traded a charcoal tomb-rubbing to Garrick the Fence in Shadow Alley for cheese and dry blankets."

4. Garrick the Fence (Cobbler's Lane & Shadow Alley)
Trigger: Shadow Alley cellar barter / DC 14 Thieves' Tools or 100 gp.

"Yeah, I kept Jonas's charcoal rubbing in my strongbox. It shows Stanza III's couplet ('South: sunken tombs of sand reveal / Two traded souls a touch must heal') and a map sketch of Zahir's camp at Hex (14, 12) leading to the Sunken Necropolis at Hex (12, 16), where the full Inversion Rite is carved in solid gold!"

5. Sister Althea (The High Hall of Lathander)
Trigger: Ask about the theological origin of the prophecy.

"Jonas's chants echo the forbidden 'Hymn of the Sundered Halos.' Our texts warn that an archdevil trapped in an angelic vessel will outwardly appear radiant and holy, while its heart burns with malicious mockery."

6. Ulcaster Ruins (Hex 11, 14) $\rightarrow$ Sunken Necropolis (Hex 12, 16)
Trigger: Explore Ulcaster Scriptorium (Hex 11, 14) & defeat Boss 2 at Hex (12, 16).

The Ulcaster Scriptorium at Hex (11, 14) provides the translation cipher for Netherese solar-hieroglyphs, allowing the party to read the Golden Alabaster Tablets (Stanzas II–VI) inside Boss 2's Suncophagus Chamber at Hex (12, 16)—proving the Angel/Devil body swap, naming the Rakshasa, and unlocking +2 to tactical checks against the final boss!

7. Prophet Joshua & The Western Sea Caves (Hex 4, 10)
Trigger: Track bandits to Hex (4, 10) at low tide (06:00–10:00 AM) or interrogate Harbor Master.

"The false sun will burn the land, but the sea cannot burn!" Terrified by prophetic dreams of the 18:00 PM solar detonation, Joshua was duped by Scribe Vane's 500 gp bounty into scuttling the caravel to 'drown the skies.' Parleying with Joshua (DC 13 Insight / DC 14 Persuasion) reveals Vane's deception and yields the Abyssal Winch Key to save Storm Giant Otheus!

Chanted at 06:00 AM by Municipal Well • Complete Codex recovered in Sunken Necropolis (Hex 12, 16)
